# JWT Authentication in FastAPI

Citation-backed analysis of JWT authentication patterns, library choices,
security pitfalls, enterprise IdP integration, and testing strategies for
FastAPI applications.

## TL;DR

**Use PyJWT** (FastAPI's official recommendation since May 2024). Pin your
algorithm (`algorithms=["RS256"]`). Use dependency injection, not middleware.
Algorithm confusion is the most exploited JWT vulnerability class — three CVEs
scored 8.2-9.3 in 2026 alone.

## Key Findings

| Decision | Recommendation | Source |
|----------|---------------|--------|
| JWT library | PyJWT 2.12.1 with `[crypto]` | FastAPI official [1][8] |
| Validation pattern | Dependency injection (not middleware) | FastAPI docs [1] |
| Algorithm | RS256 for IdP integration, HS256 for single-service | OWASP [4] |
| Token refresh | Rotation (RFC 9700 mandated for public clients) | IETF [14] |
| Token storage | Access in JS memory, refresh in httpOnly cookie | OWASP [4][23] |
| Revocation | Short-lived access + rotation + Redis denylist | [4][14][17] |
| Testing | Token factory with RSA key pairs for integration tests | [19][21] |

## Quick Decision Framework

1. **Library?** PyJWT. Avoid python-jose (CVE history, maintenance gap).
2. **Algorithm?** RS256 if any external IdP; HS256 only for internal single-service.
3. **How to validate?** FastAPI dependency injection with pinned algorithm,
   validated iss/aud/exp claims.
4. **How to test?** Dependency override for unit tests; RSA token factory for
   integration tests.
5. **How to revoke?** Short-lived access tokens (15-30 min) + refresh token
   rotation + Redis denylist for immediate revocation.
